item.description: This document uses a clockwork analogy to explain the distinction between functional principle, positional execution, external comparison and numerical representation.It illustrates continued genealogy, reproduced positions and new closures while keeping presentation separate from inspection.The analogy supports understanding. It supplies no derivation, computational evidence or validation result.A clockwork mechanism can be described before it is set in motion. Its description specifies the relations between its parts and how their operation continues.Within this analogy, P.B.F. corresponds to the functional principle underlying the mechanism. The sequence presents how that principle establishes and continues relational positions.The principle is therefore distinct from an individual gear or a particular execution.A description can explain the expected operation. An execution record can be traced back through the operations that produced it.Tracing a result back to its source is inspection, not reverse generation from a known target.The description and execution remain distinct: neither substitutes for the other.The establishment of a relational structure differs from its subsequent operation.The first concerns how positions and differentiated relations arise. The second concerns how an already established position continues under the defined operation.In the mechanical image, establishing an engagement point and moving from that point are different tasks.A subsequent position does not require a new primary principle merely because it is new. The defined operation can continue through further positions.The analogy illustrates this distinction. It does not independently establish the correspondence between a conceptual definition and executable code.K7 uses states, positional sequences, repeated operations and active genealogical references rather than physical gears.A reference advances through sequential endpoints. Its next endpoint is retained as execution continues.Within the analogy, this resembles a movement that retains its place rather than starting again whenever another portion of the field is examined.Segment boundaries divide memory allocation. They do not divide the execution into independent genealogies.The mechanical image describes continuity within K7. It does not imply that K.6, K7 and K.8 form a runtime pipeline or consume one another's output.Imagine observation positions marked along a track. Earlier references advance through that track according to their defined steps.A new closure can serve as a reference in the continued genealogy according to the implemented mechanism.Closure does not mean that the whole process stops. It identifies a local positional state from which further operation can proceed.The same operation continues while the set of established references develops.A separate disk bearing reference marks can be placed over a completed positional pattern to compare their locations.This represents the role of the independent conventional prime reference in K7.The checking disk does not drive the internal mechanism or choose its closure positions.Two preparation stages must remain distinct: The conventional base reference is prepared independently before segment execution. The comparison bitmap for a segment is constructed after the corresponding internal segment is complete. No external reference data is passed into the internal generator.The comparison asks whether the completed positional structures agree. Two disks can contain equal numbers of marks while placing them differently, so matching totals alone are insufficient.The executed comparison concerns positions throughout the declared finite domain.A clock face provides markings through which a position can be read. Those markings do not create the movement they display.Similarly, Base 10 represents already established rational values.For example:The fractional value is the source. The decimal string is its encoding. Exact reconstruction checks that the encoding preserves the value.In the analogy, this resembles reading a marked position and recovering the same position from that reading.Changing the representation does not change the informational origin of the represented relation.Presenting a mechanism and inspecting it are separate activities.Presentation does not perform the inspection. Inspection does not construct missing parts on behalf of the mechanism.The externally given Riemann position is the target statement to which the proposed construction is related. The checking-disk analogy concerns K7's prime-reference comparison; it does not establish that final relation or determine the Riemann Hypothesis.The clockwork model explains different informational roles through familiar mechanical objects.It does not establish a literal physical mechanism, prove correspondence between conceptual and computational operations, or extend finite execution beyond its recorded scope.The governing definitions, executable operations and recorded evidence determine the claims. BINARY STRUCTURE -> BASE 10 PROJECTION LOCK VALIDATOR ============================================================ Version: 2.0.0 PURPOSE ------- Test the final projection boundary: BINARY / RELATIONAL STRUCTURE ↓ PROJECTION ONLY ↓ BASE 10 REPRESENTATION The validator does NOT use Base 10 to generate the relational state. It first generates the exact relational families from binary scale expansion: 1/2 3/4 ↔ 1/4 1/8 through repeated x2 scaling. Only AFTER each exact Fraction state has been generated is it projected into Base 10. The Base 10 representation is then decoded back to an exact Fraction. LOCK CONDITION -------------- PASS requires all of the following: 1. Binary generation occurs before Base 10 projection. 2. The exact rational state is unchanged by projection. 3. Base 10 -> Fraction reconstruction returns the original state exactly. 4. Equivalent binary-scale representations map to the same Base 10 value. 5. The complement relation remains exact: active + lock = full frame 6. No new relational state is introduced by Base 10 encoding. 7. 1/4 and 1/8 are represented exactly as downstream decimal projections. No floating-point arithmetic is used. No tolerance is used. OUTPUT ------ Creates: 2. OUTPUT/ containing: K8.C_CONTROL.txt K8.C_DATA.json K8.C_REPORT.md """ from __future__ import annotations import json from datetime import datetime from fractions import Fraction from pathlib import Path from typing import Dict, List, Tuple PYTHON_CODE_ID = "K8. C" FILE_NAME = "K8. C.py" OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE = "K8. P.B.F. BINARY STRUCTURE → BASE 10 PROJECTION LOCK VALIDATOR" VERSION = "2.0.0" OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = "2. OUTPUT" DATA_FILE = "K8.C_DATA.json" REPORT_FILE = "K8.C_REPORT.md" CONTROL_FILE = "K8.C_CONTROL.txt" LEVEL_COUNT = 8 def base_dir() -> Path: """Return the validator's own directory, independent of terminal CWD.""" try: return Path(__file__).resolve().parent except NameError: return Path.cwd() # ============================================================================ # EXACT BASE-10 ENCODING / DECODING # ============================================================================ def fraction_to_decimal_exact(value: Fraction) -> str: """ Convert a Fraction to an exact finite Base-10 decimal. This validator deliberately uses binary-generated denominators whose reduced form contains only factors 2 and/or 5, so the Base-10 expansion must terminate exactly. Raises ValueError if a non-terminating decimal would be required. """ n = value.numerator d = value.denominator sign = "-" if n < 0 else "" n = abs(n) # Determine whether the reduced denominator terminates in Base 10. test_d = d while test_d % 2 == 0: test_d //= 2 while test_d % 5 == 0: test_d //= 5 if test_d != 1: raise ValueError( f"{value} does not have a finite exact Base-10 representation" ) integer_part = n // d remainder = n % d if remainder == 0: return f"{sign}{integer_part}" digits: List[str] = [] while remainder: remainder *= 10 digit = remainder // d remainder %= d digits.append(str(digit)) return f"{sign}{integer_part}." + "".join(digits) def decimal_exact_to_fraction(text: str) -> Fraction: """ Decode a finite decimal string into an exact Fraction. """ text = text.strip() sign = -1 if text.startswith("-") else 1 if text[0] in "+-": text = text[1:] if "." not in text: return Fraction(sign * int(text), 1) integer_part, fractional_part = text.split(".", 1) if not fractional_part: return Fraction(sign * int(integer_part), 1) scale = 10 ** len(fractional_part) numerator = int(integer_part) * scale + int(fractional_part) return Fraction(sign * numerator, scale) # ============================================================================ # BINARY / RELATIONAL SOURCE GENERATION # ============================================================================ def expanded_fraction(base_num: int, base_den: int, level: int) -> Tuple[int, int]: factor = 2 ** level return base_num * factor, base_den * factor def build_level(level: int) -> Dict[str, object]: """ Generate all source states BEFORE any Base-10 projection. It is processed as consecutive segments. Active genealogical references carry their next sequential endpoint from one segment into the next. Thus domain size is decoupled from RAM size. Validation architecture ----------------------- For every segment: 1. Generate the locked P.B.F. observation field. 2. Apply internally generated genealogical references by sequential endpoint continuation. 3. Produce the P.B.F. closure bitmap for that segment. 4. Only then build an independent conventional reference bitmap. 5. Compare both bitmaps byte-for-byte. A scale can PASS only if every segment through that scale is an exact positional match. Equal counts alone are NOT sufficient. Submission status ----------------- PASS requires exact byte-for-byte positional identity, zero false positives, zero false negatives, and exact observation-count agreement throughout the executed domain. Automatic checkpoints preserve the completed sequential state during the long execution. If the process is restarted, the same file resumes from the latest valid completed segment. Two principal segment bitmaps plus transient slice # buffers normally remain within a practical desktop-memory range. DEFAULT_SEGMENT_SIZE = 30_000_000 # Standard local execution output directory. OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = "2. OUTPUT" # Standard short output filenames. DATA_FILE = "K7_DATA.json" FINAL_REPORT_FILE = "K7_REPORT.md" DATA_SHEET_FILE = "K7_DATA_SHEET.md" CSV_FILE = "K7_DATA_SHEET.csv" CONTROL_FILE = "K7_CONTROL.txt" EXECUTION_FILE = "K7_EXECUTION.log" ERROR_FILE = "K7_ERROR.log" CHECKPOINT_FILE = "K7_CHECKPOINT.json" CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SEGMENTS = 25 def base_dir() -> Path: try: return Path(__file__).resolve().parent except NameError: return Path.cwd() def now_iso() -> str: return _dt.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds") def now_text() -> str: return _dt.datetime.now().astimezone().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z") def write_json(path: Path, payload) -> None: path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8") def write_json_atomic(path: Path, payload) -> None: """Write a recoverable state file without exposing a partial checkpoint.""" temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp") write_json(temporary, payload) os.replace(temporary, path) def write_text(path: Path, lines: Iterable[str]) -> None: path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8") # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # EXACT LOCKED OBSERVATION COUNT # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def fixed_observation_count_exact(limit: int) -> int: """Exact cardinality of the locked field generated by 2, 3, then 6k±1.""" if limit < 2: return 0 count = 1 if limit >= 3: count += 1 if limit >= 5: count += (limit + 1) // 6 count += max(0, (limit - 1) // 6) return count # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # INTERNAL REFERENCE GENERATION # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def build_locked_reference_field(limit: int) -> bytearray: field = bytearray(limit + 1) if limit >= 2: field[2] = 1 if limit >= 3: field[3] = 1 center = 6 while center <= limit + 1: left = center - 1 right = center + 1 if 5 <= left <= limit: field[left] = 1 if 5 <= right <= limit: field[right] = 1 center += 6 return field def project_internal_genealogy(reference: int, limit: int, field: bytearray, hit: bytearray) -> None: x = reference + reference while x <= limit: if field[x]: hit[x] = 1 x += reference def generate_internal_references(limit: int) -> List[int]: """ Generate all P.B.F. closures through `limit` with the original K7 mechanism. This is NOT an external prime list. It is generated internally from the same fixed field + sequential addition + coincidence rules used by the original benchmark. """ field = build_locked_reference_field(limit) hit = bytearray(limit + 1) closures: List[int] = [] for p in (2, 3): if p <= limit and field[p]: closures.append(p) project_internal_genealogy(p, limit, field, hit) position = 5 while position <= limit: if field[position]: if not hit[position]: closures.append(position) project_internal_genealogy(position, limit, field, hit) position += 1 return closures # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # SEGMENTED P.B.F. GENEALOGICAL ENGINE # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def fill_locked_observation_segment( low: int, high: int, next_left: int, next_right: int, ) -> Tuple[bytearray, int, int, int]: """ Build exactly the same locked observation field inside [low, high]. next_left / next_right carry the next sequential 6-step endpoints across segment boundaries. No modulo classification is used. """ size = high - low + 1 field = bytearray(size) if low <= 2 <= high: field[2 - low] = 1 if low <= 3 <= high: field[3 - low] = 1 # center-1 stream: 5, 11, 17, ... if next_left < low: while next_left < low: next_left += 6 if next_left <= high: start = next_left - low count = len(range(start, size, 6)) field[start:size:6] = b"\x01" * count next_left += count * 6 # center+1 stream: 7, 13, 19, ... if next_right < low: while next_right < low: next_right += 6 if next_right <= high: start = next_right - low count = len(range(start, size, 6)) field[start:size:6] = b"\x01" * count next_right += count * 6 return field, int(sum(field)), next_left, next_right def apply_genealogy_segment( field: bytearray, low: int, high: int, references: List[int], next_hits: List[int], ) -> None: """ Continue every internally generated genealogy through this segment. item.description: This package provides a segmented P.B.F. positional genealogy generator and an independent positional comparison.It constructs the locked observation field, applies internally generated genealogical references through sequential endpoint continuation, and records the surviving closure positions.Each completed internal segment is compared byte for byte with a separately constructed conventional prime-reference segment.This README explains the local mechanism, execution parameters, recovery procedure, evidence files and recorded results.The local package is K.7 CODE & OUTPUT.The implemented sequence is:Locked observation field → sequential addition → genealogical coincidence → reproduced position or new closure.The program processes consecutive segments from position through the requested maximum limit, inclusive. Smaller requested limits are cumulative milestones within the same continuous execution.The default maximum is:No output from another K.6, K.7 or K.8 script is required.The observation streams are:Their construction advances sequential endpoints by .At each cumulative limit:generate_internal_references() constructs the locked observation field through the reference horizon.It accepts the initial positions and , then scans the field in ascending order. An unhit observation position becomes a new reference. Its genealogy begins at and advances by , marking coincidences.During segmented execution: fill_locked_observation_segment() marks the local observation field. apply_genealogy_segment() clears genealogical endpoints using the internally generated references. Surviving marked positions form the segment's closure result. Observation endpoints and each reference's next genealogical endpoint continue into the following segment. Stepped byte-array slice operations implement these endpoint sequences.Internal classification uses observation-field membership and genealogical hits. Genealogy starts at .Segment boundaries manage memory; they do not restart the genealogy.The comparison has two preparation stages:The conventional reference uses a sieve with the start rule and integer alignment of multiples at segment boundaries.The internal generator receives its own references. Conventional reference data is passed separately to the comparison functions.The complete arrays are compared directly:segment_exact = pbf_field == reference_field If a mismatch occurs, the program scans the differing segment to count false positives and false negatives and locate the first deviation.Matching counts alone do not satisfy the positional control.For , the implemented exact observation count is:Smaller limits are handled separately.The first deviation is recorded as a position, or as null in JSON and NONE in the report when no deviation occurs.Use Python 3 with the standard-library modules imported by the source. The supplied execution metadata records Python 3.11.9 on Windows.No third-party packages, external datasets or network access are required. Both reference sets are generated locally.The default segment size is integer positions. Each principal byte array occupies approximately MB for a full segment. Temporary slice buffers, reference lists, trace records and checkpoint data require additional memory.The complete domain is processed in segments rather than allocated as one array.The supplied run records approximately minutes of segmented execution. Runtime depends on the machine and selected parameters.Run these commands from the local package root.Complete default milestone sequence:python "1. Python/K7.py" Smaller domain:python "1. Python/K7.py" --limits 1000000 Selected milestones and segment size:python "1. Python/K7.py" --limits 1000000 10000000 --segment-size 1000000 Write directly to the package-level output folder:python "1. Python/K7.py" --output-dir "2. OUTPUT" Use python3 where that is the Python executable name.Limits are sorted and deduplicated. The engine retains limits of at least , and requires at least one such limit. The CLI rejects limits above .The minimum accepted segment size is . Segments are shortened where necessary to end exactly at a milestone or the maximum limit.On Windows, an interactive terminal waits for Enter before closing.Without --output-dir, the script writes beside itself:1. Python/2. OUTPUT/The supplied records are stored in:2. OUTPUT/A supplied report copy is stored in:3. FINAL REPORTS/Use --output-dir "2. OUTPUT" from the package root to write to the package-level output folder.An explicit relative output path is resolved from the terminal's working directory. The default path is resolved from the script's location.The script prints the actual output directory. It does not automatically copy the report into 3. FINAL REPORTS.Repeated execution uses the same output filenames.During continued execution, K7_CHECKPOINT.json is written after every completed segments.It records: the next segment position; observation and genealogical endpoints; cumulative diagnostics; milestone results; segment trace; elapsed execution time. Checkpoint writing uses a temporary file followed by replacement to avoid exposing a partially written checkpoint.Restart with the same output directory, milestone limits, segment size and program version. The loader checks these settings and the internal reference count before restoring state.Execution resumes from the latest saved completed segment. Work performed after that checkpoint is repeated.After successful final output writing, the checkpoint is removed. A later run starts a fresh execution.A configuration mismatch raises an error rather than restoring incompatible state.Six final files are written. Checkpoint and error files serve execution-state functions.Each trace entry records segment boundaries, observation count, closure count, conventional reference count, positional agreement, false positives, false negatives and duration.The records retain counts and comparison results. Complete segment byte arrays are released after comparison and are not retained.The supplied reports in 2. OUTPUT and 3. FINAL REPORTS contain the same report text and recorded results.The supplied records identify completion at:2026-09-29T06:52:43+02:00All six cumulative milestones record exact positional agreement, zero false positives, zero false negatives and matching observation counts.The execution time covers the segmented stage. Reference-generation times are recorded separately.Caught execution errors are written to K7_ERROR.log.Command-line parsing and some preliminary validation occur before that handler. Errors at those stages may terminate without producing this file.After an interrupted or failed run, inspect the execution log, error log and checkpoint. Previously completed final files may remain until a later run replaces them. Inspect 1. Python/K7.py for observation-field construction, internal reference generation and endpoint continuation.
